description: Add a recurring issue to a project, or change the one named by 'id' — the WHOLE of it as you write it here: what you leave out of a change is cleared, not kept. From 'nextDay' on, every 'every' weeks or months, the project files this issue at nine in the morning on YOUR clock and in YOUR name: with your access, through the same rules, notifications and watchers as an issue you filed yourself. In 'summary', {date}, {month}, {quarter} and {year} are read off the day it is filed ('VAT return {quarter}' → 'VAT return Q4 2026'). If the one filed before is still open, the new one is filed all the same and linked to it. A day missed — a paused project — files once when it can, never a backlog. Refused, with the reason, if the issue could not be filed as described today (an unknown type, an assignee nobody has). The project's lead, the company's owner or an admin only.

assignee.description: Assignee username or e-mail. Nobody where nothing is said.

description.description: The filed issue's description, Markdown; [~username] mentions notify each time.

dueInDays.description: The filed issue's due day, as a number of days after the day it is filed — 19 makes an issue filed on the 1st due on the 20th. A count, not a day of the month. Leave out for no due day.

enabled.description: false to keep it switched off. Default true.

every.description: Every how many units: 1 (the default), 3 for a quarter, 12 for a year. Up to 52 weeks or 24 months.

id.description: The schedule to change, as list_issue_schedules returned it. Leave out to add one.

nextDay.description: The first day it files on, YYYY-MM-DD, today or later on your clock. For months, its day of the month is the day kept (the 31st is a short month's last day).

summary.description: The filed issue's title; {date}, {month}, {quarter}, {year} are filled in on the day.

type.description: Issue type name, one of the project's. 'Task' where nothing is said.

name: set_issue_schedule
